nodes.label: No-JavaScript Link-Based Filtering
nodes.rationale: Every filter is a real link to a real URL, so it is shareable, bookmarkable, crawlable and works on a bad connection.

nodes.label: Archive Moved to Theme Root
nodes.rationale: The template lived in templates/, a directory the WordPress template hierarchy never looks in, and called a template part that was never written, so the archive silently fell through to index.php.

nodes.label: Video Fetched as Blob, Not Streamed
nodes.rationale: Many hosts lack HTTP Range support; without it every seek clamps to zero, so scrubbing works on localhost and does nothing live. A Blob works everywhere.

nodes.label: Coalesced Seek Gate
nodes.rationale: Writing currentTime while a previous seek is in flight piles seeks up; gating and coalescing to the newest is the difference between smooth and choppy in Chrome. An error handler releases the gate because a failed seek never fires seeked.

nodes.label: Frame-Delta Normalised Easing
nodes.rationale: A flat per-frame constant converges twice as fast on 120Hz as on 60Hz, making the site feel like a different site per machine.

nodes.label: Five Live Static-Hero Media Gates
nodes.rationale: Deciding once at load leaves a blank multi-viewport hero the moment a tablet rotates or reduced motion is switched off mid-session, so the gates listen live.

nodes.label: Chunk-Rearmed Download Watchdog
nodes.rationale: The watchdog measures stalls, not total download time: a slow connection is fine, a dead one is not, so it re-arms on every chunk and falls back to a static hero on abort.

nodes.label: Monotonic Repeater Row Index
nodes.rationale: The save handler reindexes and drops blank rows, so the index only needs uniqueness; a counter that never goes backwards avoids the collision you get from using the current row count after a middle row was removed.

nodes.label: Disabled Repeater Template Row
nodes.rationale: The template ships with disabled inputs so the browser never submits it; a cloned real row must have disabled stripped or it saves as nothing.

nodes.label: Save-Data / Motion / Width Video Gate
nodes.rationale: An autoplaying video with a real src downloads the whole file before first paint regardless of preload, so the URL ships in data-tk-video-src and is only attached above 768px, with a poster, when the connection is not slow or save-data.

nodes.label: PHP Parse-Error Guard Script
nodes.rationale: A WordPress theme has no build step, so a PHP parse error is caught by nothing before it reaches the server, where it shows up as a white screen on the live site.

nodes.label: Server-Side-Only Mail Recipient
nodes.rationale: The recipient used to be a hidden input read from $_POST, making the site an open relay on its own domain and SMTP reputation. The nonce was no defence because nonces are embedded in the public page HTML.

nodes.label: Sixty-Second stale-while-revalidate Window
nodes.rationale: A day-long stale window is honoured by browsers on navigation, so a returning visitor keeps the old TEMPLATE while every stylesheet updates by URL — presenting as 'only the colours and fonts changed'. max-age=0 plus s-maxage keeps the CDN win; 60s caps the staleness.

nodes.label: ?ver= Cache Busting Preserved
nodes.rationale: A removed tk_remove_query_strings() filter stripped ?ver= from asset URLs — an old scoring trick that is free on HTTP/2 but defeats TRIP_KAILASH_VERSION cache busting, leaving stale CSS after every deploy.

nodes.label: tk_filter_packages_by_tradition
nodes.rationale: Guarded on the main front-end query so it cannot reach into the admin, a feed, or any secondary loop a widget happens to run.

nodes.label: Doors Sit Above the Packages
nodes.rationale: Reframes what the visitor thinks they are shopping for before a price appears; once someone is comparing $350 to $1,000 the pilgrimage framing is gone and the site competes on cost with all of Thamel.

nodes.label: Empty Traditions Are Not Shown
nodes.rationale: Driven by the tradition taxonomy so a door cannot describe a catalogue that has moved on; an empty door reads as a hole, and a path leading nowhere is worse than one fewer path.

nodes.label: Kailash Forced Last
nodes.rationale: A design decision, not an ordering preference, so it is enforced in code rather than left to menu_order where one drag would undo it. The flagship has never sold; putting it first asks a stranger for $2,500 before the site has earned anything.

nodes.label: Sacred Meaning, Never Logistics
nodes.rationale: Every competitor leads with logistics, which is exactly why this leads with meaning; the facts sit in a small row underneath.

nodes.label: Pinning Disabled Below 900px
nodes.rationale: Pinned scroll-jacking on phones is reliably awful and most of this traffic is phones, so the track becomes a native horizontal swipe with scroll-snap.

nodes.label: Altitude and Overnight on Every Day
nodes.rationale: Pilgrims who skip acclimatisation are the ones turned back below the pass, so a day list that hides where you sleep and how high hides the thing that decides whether the trip works.

nodes.label: details/summary Accordion, No JS
nodes.rationale: Built on details and summary so it works with no JavaScript and keyboard support is the browser's rather than ours.

nodes.label: Colour Is Not the Only Signal
nodes.rationale: Good months are also labelled and announced, so the bar works for a colour-blind reader and a screen reader both. A prose sentence like 'March to May and September to November' makes the reader turn text back into a calendar.

nodes.label: Three Caches In Front Of The Site
nodes.rationale: LiteSpeed, Hostinger's regional hcdn edge, and the visitor's browser honouring stale-while-revalidate are three separate caches with three separate purge controls. Every check a developer runs (curl, hard refresh, ?query= URL) is a different cache key and returns the correct page while the reporter still sees the old one.

nodes.label: Cache-Layer Diagnosis via curl
nodes.rationale: x-hcdn-cache-status HIT with a non-zero Age means you are looking at the edge, not the site; a never-requested ?bust= URL is a fresh key all the way down and shows what the server actually renders.

nodes.label: Elementor _wp_page_template Override
nodes.rationale: Page 11 had elementor_header_footer stored in _wp_page_template; Elementor hooks template_include late and returns its own template, which beats front-page.php outright. The theme loaded and home.css was on the page — the template just never ran. Fix was setting _wp_page_template to default.

nodes.label: Group Pricing Quoted the Wrong Rate
nodes.rationale: price_from is the marketing figure, normally the largest group's rate. The old logic started at the headline and only moved lower, so a solo pilgrim was quoted the ten-person rate ($350 instead of $650).

nodes.label: Phase 2.5 Content Migration Over MCP
nodes.rationale: Gradings, durations and altitudes had drifted from duplicated pages. Taxonomy terms could not be assigned because the theme that registers them was not deployed yet, which is why Muktinath was filed under Shiva rather than Vaishnava and Buddhist.

nodes.label: Manual Theme Upload to Hostinger
nodes.rationale: The MCP connector can write content, fields, terms and menus but not theme PHP/CSS/JS, and CI only syntax-checks, so files reach the server by git checkout or SFTP. Directory capitalisation matters because WordPress resolves the theme by directory name on a case-sensitive host.

nodes.label: Elementor Canvas Full-Width Setup
nodes.rationale: Content width 100%, zero widget spacing, zero section/column padding and the Elementor Canvas page layout are what remove the white gutters around a full-bleed hero.

nodes.label: Regenerate CSS and Clear All Caches
nodes.rationale: White space that persists after correct settings is usually cached CSS or inline styles: regenerate Elementor CSS, then clear browser, WordPress and CDN caches.

hyperedges.label: The deploy is correct and the site looks unchanged
hyperedges.note: HTML held by three independent caches while assets refresh by ?ver= URL, producing 'only the colours and fonts changed'. Only meaningful as a seven-way flow: the header directive, the version key, the three cache layers, the curl diagnosis, and the build guard.

hyperedges.label: Scrubbed hero: gate, fetch, seek, caption
hyperedges.note: One contract spanning PHP markup (data-video/data-poster/data-bytes, .tk-band data-from/data-to), a character-identical media-query list duplicated in CSS, and the JS drive loop. Breaking any one member silently blanks or freezes the hero.

hyperedges.label: Tradition taxonomy drives the whole catalogue path
hyperedges.note: A single ?tradition=<slug> query arg is produced by the doors and filter links, consumed by pre_get_posts and by the archive's own $_GET read, validated against terms registered at init:0 and seeded at init:5, and counted by tk_tradition_count to decide which doors render at all.
